source.check: 24 divisions, 25 seats (Newtownabbey two). Unopposed names and divisions from the returning officer's notice of result (Belfast Newsletter, 6 June 1964, p. 10); votes for the three contested divisions from the Belfast Telegraph, 5 June 1964, p. 4.

note: Triennial election of Antrim County Council. The official notice (Irish News, 7 May 1964, p. 2) fixed the day of election as Thursday 4 June 1964; nomination day was Tuesday 19 May and withdrawals closed at 5 p.m. on Wednesday 20 May. Three divisions went to a poll on 4 June: Ballymoney, Carrickfergus and Newtownabbey. The returning officer's 'County of Antrim: notice of result of elections, 1964' (Belfast Newsletter, 6 June 1964, p. 10) names the member elected for every division, including the twenty-one returned unopposed; it also prints Finaghy, which the earlier nomination notice had omitted. Printed: 'Newtownabbey - Two seats. Thomas Kerr (U.), 3,245; Robert James Kidd (Lab.), 2,726; Robert McMurtry (Lab.), 2,455; Herbert Robinson (U.), 3,152. Two Unionists elected. Twenty-eight pc poll. Spoiled votes 11.' The notice of poll gives the same four candidates and their descriptions: Kerr (manager), Kidd (building worker), McMurtry (insurance agent) and Robinson (company director). No electorate or total poll is printed.
